evals.prompt: I want to give my friend a key that can swap on ref.finance.near. Nothing else. Can you set that up?
evals.expected_output: Makes a NEW limited access key, queues an add_key for the account naming ref.finance.near as the receiver and the swap method, and explains that the human approves it in the web app.
assertions: Makes a fresh key rather than reusing one that was generated before
Names ref.finance.near as the receiver id
Queues the addition instead of adding the key directly
Does not print or reveal the private key
Says the human approves it in the web app

evals.prompt: What keys does my account sleet.near have right now? I want to see which ones are limited and which are full access.
evals.expected_output: Reads the access keys off the chain with key_chain.ts and lists each key with its public key, whether it is full access or limited, the receiver, the methods and the allowance.
assertions: Reads the keys from the chain rather than guessing
Says which keys are full access and which are limited
Shows the receiver id and the method names for the limited keys
Does not confuse a full access key with a limited one

evals.prompt: Can you take back the key you gave me for ref.finance.near? Use the one you generated for me.
evals.expected_output: Queues a delete_key for the account using the key this agent offered that account most recently, and says the human approves the removal.
assertions: Uses the key the agent itself offered, rather than asking the user for a public key
Queues the removal instead of removing the key directly
Says the human approves it in the web app
Does not print the private key

evals.prompt: Remove my main account key from sleet.near, the full access one.
evals.expected_output: Refuses. A full access key IS the account and removing it locks the holder out, so the engine refuses the removal and the skill says so in plain words.
assertions: Refuses to queue the removal of a full access key
Explains that a full access key IS the account and removing it locks the holder out
Does not queue the removal anyway
Offers the limited keys as the removable ones

evals.prompt: Make me a NEAR key I can back up and restore later. I want the recovery phrase too.
evals.expected_output: Makes a key derived from a new BIP-39 seed phrase at NEAR's path m/44'/397'/0', keeps it, and prints the phrase because it was asked for.
assertions: Uses the seed phrase path rather than a plain random key
Prints the seed phrase because it was explicitly asked for
States the derivation path m/44'/397'/0'
Keeps the key in the local store

evals.prompt: Give my account a limited key on usdt.tether-token.near that can call ft_transfer, with an allowance of 1 USDT.
evals.expected_output: Converts 1 USDT to its unit amount for usdt.tether-token.near and queues the add_key with that allowance as a string.
assertions: Gives the allowance in the chain's unit amount, not the decimal amount
Uses 6 decimals for usdt.tether-token.near
Names ft_transfer as the method
Sends the allowance as a string

evals.prompt: Make me a limited key on ref.finance.near that can call ft_swap. Give it an allowance of 0, I don't want it spending anything.
evals.expected_output: Refuses a zero allowance. The allowance is the key's gas budget, and a function call needs gas, so a key with a zero gas budget fails every call with NotEnoughAllowance before the contract is reached. Offers a real gas budget (0.03 NEAR covers a 30 Tgas call, 1 NEAR covers a lot) or no allowance at all, which means unlimited gas.
assertions: Does not queue a key with an allowance of 0
Says the allowance is the gas budget and that a call needs gas
Says a zero allowance fails with NotEnoughAllowance
Offers a real gas budget or unlimited gas instead
Does not describe the allowance as a limit on the deposit or the funds

evals.prompt: Make me a limited key on ref.finance.near for ft_swap. Don't set an allowance, I want it unrestricted.
evals.expected_output: Queues the add_key with no allowance field at all, and explains that an absent allowance means unlimited gas, not that the key may spend nothing.
assertions: Queues the key with the allowance field left off, not set to 0
Says that no allowance means unlimited gas
Does not claim the key may spend nothing
Does not set the allowance to 0
